title.narrative: Forum Fisheries Agency: Pacific Islands Regional Oceanscape Program - Second Phase for Economic Resilience

description.narrative: The Development Objective of the Series of Projects is to strengthen the shared management of selected Pacific Island oceanic and coastal fisheries, and the critical habitats upon which they depend.For FFA's second phase Project ('FFA PROPER'), the Project Development Objective (PDO) is to strengthen regional capacity for management and sustainable development of the oceanic fisheries sector in Selected Pacific Island Countries.Targeted FFA member countries include: Federated States of Micronesia, Independent State ofPapua New Guinea, Independent State of Samoa, Kingdom of Tonga, Nauru, Palau, Republic of Fiji, Republic of Kiribati, Republic of the Marshall Islands, Republic of Vanuatu, Solomon Islands, and Tuvalu.

The development objective of Forum Fisheries Agency (FFA) : Pacific Islands Regional Oceanscape Program - Second Phase for Economic Resilience Project for Pacific Islands is to strengthen the shared management of selected Pacific Island oceanic and coastal fisheries, and the critical habitats upon which they depend. This project has four components. 1) The first component, Consolidating oceanic fisheries management, has the following sub-components: (i) Identifying, quantifying and reducing risks of IUU fishing in oceanic fisheries; and (ii) Enhancing the fisheries management capacity of Targeted FFA Members. 2) The second component, Harnessing economic benefits of oceanic fisheries to the regional economy, has the following sub-components: (i) Modelling and forecasting economic and social benefits of fisheries development; and (ii) Improving investment climate and negotiation capacity. 3) The third component, Strengthening FFA's operating environment, has the following sub-components: (i) Low carbon transition for FFA's infrastructure; (ii) Strengthening FFA's cybersecurity, cloud business continuity, and business planning and accounting; and (iii) Engaging citizens on the regional importance of fisheries. 4) The fourth component, Project Management, aims to finance the Project Management Unit (PMU) to implement and manage the project, including staffing and operation of said unit to conduct monitoring and evaluation, environmental and social risk management, and financial and procurement management.

Most of the activities aimed at achieving this indicator are almost complete. The FFA off-site back up support, the encryption and single sign in consultancy are currently ongoing, due for completion by the end of June 2025. Other activities to enhance the FFA's cybersecurity within this reporting period are the delivery of a cyber security training for the FFA staff, ongoing online courses and quizzes on cybersecurity awareness for FFA staff such as phishing, vishing, malware, multifactor authentication, social engineering and social media best practices.
Progress with upgrades to digital infrastructure critical to ensure secure access and use of data to support decision making processes of FFA and its members, e.g. improved data encryption, offsite cloud back-up, etc. preventing cyber security breaches.

title.narrative: Information Management System for IUU metrics developed and providing up-to-date information

comment.narrative:
The FFA Fisheries Operations Division (FOD) is currently progressing the FFA Regional MCS Strategy, under which the development of the dashboard for IUU reporting will be developed. The dashboard for the IUU reporting is being developed by a consulting firm, scheduled to be completed by August 2025.
Progress on technical IMS development to support collection, and analysis for IUU metrics, including further development of the Regional Information Management Framework (RIMF).

title.narrative: Number of FFA member country representatives reporting improved capacity and confidence in negotiating fisheries arrangements and agreements.

comment.narrative:
An assessment of impact will be made before the second negotiations course has been completed. The first negotiation training was completed in June 2024 and the second training was scheduled to be delivered in June 2025. The impacts of these trainings and workshops will be assessed through a survey to confirm this indicator to ascertain, how the trainings and workshops delivered have helped to improve their capacity in negotiating fisheries agreements.
Assessment of impact and application of negotiations training and information from strategic economic reports in negotiations for fisheries access agreements by FA member countries. Increased capacity and confidence is expected to result in more favorable terms for FFA member countries in agreements.

title.narrative: Number of FFA member countries reporting that fisheries-related policy making is being informed by FFA policy briefs.

comment.narrative:
There are no related PROPER funded policy briefs completed within this reporting period. In terms of progress towards the achievement of this target, there are some activities currently being implemented in relation to the East New Britain Initiative (ENBI) which will be used by Members to base policy decisions in relation to: 1) development of regional tuna hubs and spokes for the region (completed for Members review), 2) report on review and assessment of the scalability of Pacific Island Tuna model as a suitable regional enterprise to facilitate market access to USA which will provide as a basis for Members guidance and decisions.
Assessment of impact and update of recommendations and guidance from policy briefs by FFA member countries.
